activity.notes: David Ben-Gurion headed Israel's provisional government from the establishment of the state on 14 May 1948 and continued as Prime Minister through the first four governments. His first continuous prime-ministerial tenure ended on 26 January 1954, when Moshe Sharett became Prime Minister. ATLAS records this as a separate Activity because Ben-Gurion was out of the prime ministership until November 1955.

sources.title: Past Governments — Prime Minister's Office, Israel
sources.citation_text: The Israeli Prime Minister's Office records David Ben-Gurion as prime minister of the Provisional Government beginning 14 May 1948 and through the Fourth Government ending 26 January 1954.

sources.title: David Ben-Gurion — Knesset
sources.citation_text: The Knesset identifies Ben-Gurion as Israel's first Prime Minister and describes his departure from government in 1953-1954 before his later return.
